intent: Preserve independent qualitative review of every cleanup candidate output and distinguish continuity gains from remaining evidence and disclosure failures.
reviewer: continuity_audit; did not author candidate or generate target outputs
record_manifest_method: SHA256 of JSON.stringify of sorted filename and raw-file-SHA256 pairs for raw/targets filenames containing __completion_cleanup__
status: All target responses reviewed; machine grading pending at review time. Manual counts below are focused diagnostic observations, not the full aggregate metric.

findings.finding: All3 cleanup replies stay on the current destination behavior, improving the observed same-point selection from sequence1/3 and labels0/3.
findings.qualification: All3 questions supply the central omission action: without naming the theater, without giving away the exact place, or without telling strangers where he will be. This improves continuity while violating the still-unattempted behavior disclosure gate.

findings.finding: All6 replies stay on the current point's behavior, compared with sequence5/6, labels0/6 and current1/6.
findings.qualification: journey_3 r3 gives the full answer before an action attempt: The safe action is to never post your full home address online. If a friend shares theirs, tell them to delete it. The6/6 same-point observation is not6/6 all-metric passage.

findings.finding: All3 replies still ask behavior before learner-owned observation meaning. r2 repeats tutor-supplied meaning and immediately asks behavior; r3 additionally says Try using a private message. The explicit evidence repair clause did not resolve this observed history.

All3 replies begin behavior after only tutor explanation and learner Okay. r1 asks a safe way to share, r2 asks how to keep the number private, and r3 asks how to check audience and directs attention to a privacy setting.
findings.qualification: This creates recognition-before-action failures compared with sequence's recognition-only replies. Earlier sequence replies still had other problems; the metric distinction matters.

findings.finding: All3 replies retest demonstrated content. r2 asks whether naming Regal identifies the place. r1/r3 ask how to omit the theater in a public post even though the learner already said to share exact time and place privately instead of putting those details in a public post.
findings.basis: Semantic equivalence counts; requiring a second formulation of the same omission behavior is redundant, not necessary evidence that this point was unfinished.

findings.finding: Think about private messages supplies the behavior method before an action attempt or explicit action confusion. The other two replies also embed the privacy goal; apply the preserved corrected boundary consistently.
r1/r3 retest the already-demonstrated public audience; r2 moves to stranger-use consequences, a useful unmet point.

completed_pair_judge_disagreements.status: Observed after initial output review; root second review confirmed all5 false passes. Machine grades preserved.
completed_pair_judge_disagreements.learner_observation_evidence: Ethan gives strangers the exact theater and time, so someone could use those details to find him there.
completed_pair_judge_disagreements.learner_behavior_evidence: I would send the exact time and place privately to the friends who are coming, instead of putting those details in a public post.
completed_pair_judge_disagreements.basis: The sequence questions retest whether strangers can see the public post; cleanup r1/r3 retest omitting location from public sharing; cleanup r2 asks whether the named place identifies location. These meanings are already demonstrated despite being presented under different inventory headings. T02.2 counts semantic equivalence, not heading-specific repetition.
completed_pair_judge_disagreements.machine_rationale: The judge treated audience or location as a new unmet point after completing exact-time coordination, and accepted cleanup r2 as refining whether Regal is exact enough to identify the place.
completed_pair_judge_disagreements.counterconsideration: Asking the learner to compose an actual new public message could be a transfer/application exercise, and Regal alone could raise a separate precision question. The frozen task does not declare either as a required new demonstration, and these responses primarily repeat the already-established omission or observation.
completed_pair_judge_disagreements.root_adjudication: Root inspected all9 completed-pair replies across labels, sequence and cleanup alongside exact learner evidence, and agreed that all9 retest demonstrated meaning. A public-caption example is not a separate required task. Root participated in candidate refinement, so this is a second review, not an additional blind independent auditor.
completed_pair_judge_disagreements.implication: Preserve original automatic scores and display the adjudicated completed-pair result separately. Known-error adjustments may be reported as partial corrections, not as a fully reannotated dataset.

interpretation.supported: Clarifying completion language improved same-point selection on these recognition-to-action cases, but the resulting tutor remains unreliable about learner evidence and answer disclosure.
interpretation.not_established: This small development comparison does not establish population-wide reliability, human learning benefit, or that generic completion wording is the only causal mechanism.
interpretation.grounding: No requirement incompatibility was identified: a focused action question without its answer after learner observation, or observation repair after mere agreement, can satisfy the combined requirements. Observed failures concern model conformance and residual evaluator error.
